deep.reconstruction:
WHAT THE PAGE IS. The page is a table for every prime p ≡ 1 (mod 4) from 2837 down to 2377. These are exactly the primes in that range: 2837, 2833, 2801, 2797, 2789, 2777, 2753, 2749, 2741, 2729, 2713, 2693, 2689, 2677, 2657, 2633, 2621, 2617, 2609, 2593, 2557, 2549, 2521, 2477, 2473, 2441, 2437, 2417, 2393, 2389, 2381, 2377. The previous page covers the same table for 2969 down to 2857.

For each prime Gauss writes the sequence of denominators Q_k from the continued-fraction expansion of √p. In his language these are the first coefficients of the successive reduced forms (Q_k, P_k, −Q_{k+1}) of determinant p, i.e. b² − ac = p, in the principal cycle.

THE RECURRENCE (modern notation; Gauss writes only the Q's):
- Start: P_0 = 0, Q_0 = 1, a_0 = ⌊√p⌋.
- Step: a_k = ⌊(a_0 + P_k)/Q_k⌋, P_{k+1} = a_k Q_k − P_k, Q_{k+1} = (p − P_{k+1}²)/Q_k.
- Hence Q_1 = p − ⌊√p⌋². For example 2609 − 51² = 8, 2713 − 52² = 9, 2833 − 53² = 24, 2377 − 48² = 73.

The row stops at the first repetition Q_k = Q_{k+1} ('41.41 &c'). This is the centre of the palindromic period, which has odd length because p ≡ 1 (mod 4) and the norm of the fundamental unit is −1. At that point p = P_{k+1}² + Q_k². This is the continued-fraction (Legendre/Gauss) method of writing p as a sum of two squares.

Worked example, p = 2837 (a_0 = 53), as (P, Q, a) step by step:
- (53, 28, 3) → (31, 67, 1) → (36, 23, 3) → (33, 76, 1) → (43, 13, 7) → (48, 41, 2) → (34, 41).
- So the row reads 1.28.67.23.76.13.41.41, and 2837 = 34² + 41².
- The full set of partial quotients is √2837 = [53; 3,1,3,1,7,2,2,7,1,3,1,3,106].

Other rows checked by me in full: 2713, 2621, 2477, 2441, 2777, 2789, the start of 2549, and the second rows of 2621 and 2837. The terminal pairs of all rows give:
- 2833 = 48² + 23², 2801 = 20² + 49², 2797 = 14² + 51², 2789 = 50² + 17², 2777 = 44² + 29²
- 2753 = 52² + 7², 2749 = 30² + 43², 2741 = 46² + 25², 2729 = 52² + 5², 2713 = 52² + 3²
- 2693 = 22² + 47², 2689 = 40² + 33², 2677 = 34² + 39², 2657 = 16² + 49², 2633 = 28² + 43²
- 2621 = 50² + 11², 2617 = 4² + 51², 2609 = 20² + 47², 2593 = 48² + 17², 2557 = 46² + 21²
- 2549 = 50² + 7², 2521 = 36² + 35², 2477 = 46² + 19², 2473 = 48² + 13², 2441 = 40² + 29²
- 2437 = 6² + 49², 2417 = 4² + 49², 2393 = 32² + 37², 2389 = 42² + 25², 2381 = 34² + 35², 2377 = 44² + 21²

THE SECOND ROWS. Seven primes carry a second row and the marks '0.3' and '1.2': 2837, 2797, 2777, 2713, 2677, 2621 and 2557.
- These are the primes for which the number of properly primitive classes of determinant p is 3. The next page summarises exactly these primes as 'p. 3. …'; 2917 and 9 classes appear on the previous page with labels 0.9, 1.8, 2.7, 3.6, 4.5.
- The labels index classes by exponent of a generator: 0 ≡ 3 is the principal class; 1 and 2 are a class and its inverse.
- The second row is the complete cycle of Q's of the non-principal class, from a small admissible Q back to itself, e.g. 2837: 4, 7, 19, …, 59, 4. The inverse class has the same cycle read backwards.
- The starting Q is 4 or 3 when p ≡ 5 (mod 8), and 8 when p ≡ 1 (mod 8) (2777, 2713). Leading coefficients 2 and 4 would there give improperly primitive forms.
- Checks of the second rows: for 2621, the step from Q = 5 with P = 51 gives Q = 44, 25, 53, …; the cycle 4, 5, 44, …, 55, 4 has length 11. For 2837, Q = 4 → 7 requires P = 53, and the row continues 19, 52, … as written.

PURPOSE. Unmarked primes have a single (principal) cycle, i.e. class number 1. The page is raw material for Gauss's table of class numbers of binary quadratic forms with positive prime determinant (cf. Disq. Arith. art. 303–304 and the Nachlass class-number tables in Werke II), obtained by exhausting reduced forms cycle by cycle.

results.what: For every prime p ≡ 1 mod 4 with 2377 ≤ p ≤ 2837: the Q_k of the continued fraction of √p up to the symmetric centre Q_k = Q_{k+1}, giving p = P² + Q².
results.modern_name: Continued-fraction (Legendre/Serret-type) algorithm for representing a prime as a sum of two squares; principal cycle of reduced indefinite forms
results.usually_credited_to: Legendre (Essai sur la théorie des nombres, 1798); reduction-cycle form due to Gauss (Disq. Arith. 1801)

results.what: Cycles of reduced forms of non-principal classes for determinants with 3 classes, labelled by class exponent (0.3 / 1.2), identifying p = 2837, 2797, 2777, 2713, 2677, 2621, 2557 as class number 3.
results.modern_name: Computation of class numbers h(4p) of real quadratic orders via cycles of reduced forms (infrastructure); cyclic class group labelling
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Disq. Arith. art. 187–222, 303–304; class-number tables published posthumously in Werke II)

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine tabulation work for Gauss's known class-number tables of positive determinants. The method, reduced-form cycles via the continued fraction of √p, is his own published theory. The by-product, sums of two squares, is classical (Legendre/Gauss).
